text: Three separate report pages, each one answering exactly one group of Lesson 84's original requirements — genuinely not one single crowded page desperately trying to do absolutely everything at once, which would violate Chapter Eight's one-screen rule the moment real numbers actually replace placeholder data.

Page one covers territory-level sales measured directly against target, using a headline card top-left and a bar chart sorted descending rather than a map, since a sorted bar chart is genuinely more honest for precise comparison. Page two covers category and subcategory margin in full, with a bar chart sorted by the actual margin percentage rather than alphabetically. Page three covers reseller fulfillment together with year-over-year trend, side by side, using a line chart overlaying this year against last year.

Every single page follows the exact same underlying rules throughout: the headline card sits top-left and largest on every page, bars get sorted by the actual metric itself rather than lazily sorted alphabetically, and identical color conventions carry consistently across all three pages without exception — the same color for sales everywhere, the same color for target or prior year everywhere else.

Three complete pages, each with its own clear five-second headline number a viewer could name instantly without any real effort. Lesson 90 adds the real interactivity that finally lets a viewer actually explore meaningfully past that first headline number, without cluttering any of these three carefully built pages.
